Yes — very likely.

At 21° altitude, the Moon is comfortably above the horizon, though low enough that haze or buildings could matter. With a clear night sky, a 37%-illuminated Moon is easily bright enough for normal unaided vision, especially since the Sun is nearly 50° below the horizon and the sky is fully dark.

Its ~75° separation from the Sun is not a problem at night; it is far from twilight glare. Look toward azimuth 239° — roughly west-southwest — about two fist-widths above the horizon if you hold your fist at arm’s length (each fist ≈10°).

The main reasons you might *not* see it would be local obstructions, low-horizon haze/light pollution, or clouds not reflected in the “clear” report. But assuming you have an open view toward the west-southwest, it should be quite noticeable.
